target_customer: Mobile shoppers, about 80 percent female, teens and budget minded mothers aged 25 to 35 per TechCrunch in 2013; retailers as advertisers and partners
problem: Shoppers did not know about sales and coupons at nearby stores while in or near them.
business_model: Free consumer app monetized through retailer promotions, affiliate and advertising; later cash back through Ebates
product_category: Mobile coupons and deals discovery app

founders.name: Navneet Loiwal
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (Sept 2013) calls the founders former Shopkick engineers; the YC description says engineers from Google, Shopkick and Loopt, without saying who worked where. CEO title taken from TechCrunch coverage of the founder, not verified on a company page.

founders.name: Tommy Tsai
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as Tommy Sze Ngai Tsai. TechCrunch calls him a former Shopkick engineer. Education not found.

competitors.name: Shopkick
competitors.what: Rewards users for walking into stores and purchasing

competitors.name: RetailMeNot
competitors.what: Coupon site that launched its first iOS app in June 2012 and an Android app in August 2012

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed coupon and sale aggregation from over 100 retailers plus location based notifications on iOS and Android; the geofence and data work was moderate for engineers with Shopkick experience.

defensibility.rationale: Coupon aggregation and geo alerts were copyable; the CEO argued RetailMeNot's geo feature was narrower, but that is his own claim.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: RetailMeNot added mobile apps in 2012. No incumbent copy killed Shopular; Ebates bought it in March 2016.

market_need_then: Smartphone adoption and a growing coupon app field in 2012. Early traction was reported as 250,000 downloads in three weeks and 4.8 to 5 star ratings across about 10,000 reviews by 2013, per TechCrunch and Vator.

branding.domain_note: Used shopular.com, which now redirects to rakuten.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as a tap on the shoulder telling you why to walk into a store

branding.brand_signature: Time Magazine 50 best iPhone apps listing as claimed on the YC page

rebrands.why: Kept the name under Ebates after the acquisition, per press coverage.

branding.community_and_virality: No community or merch evidence found. Press on the brand was an app listing and ratings.

brand_strength.rationale: A catchy invented name and high app store ratings, plus a claimed Time list placement, but no mascot or community evidence.

outcome_analysis: Shopular came out of YC W12 with Shopkick trained engineers, soft launched in late 2012 with 250,000 downloads in three weeks, raised a 6.4 million Series A from Sequoia in September 2013 and was sold to Ebates in March 2016 at an undisclosed price. The site now redirects to Rakuten. Sources show high app ratings but no disclosed revenue, so the quality of the exit is unknown.
notes: Dealroom lists 13.7M total funding while CB Insights lists about 6.4M; only the 6.4M Series A is confirmed. Seed amount not found. Loiwal's CEO title is from press, the YC page lists only Tommy Tsai. SnipSnap was named only in a 2013 article, so it is left out of the founding competitor list.
